title: TVP vs. ground beef: nutrition compared

seo.title: TVP vs. ground beef: protein, fiber and fat
seo.meta_description: Compare textured soy protein with 90/10 ground beef using the same 20 g protein target.
seo.search_intent: Compare TVP and ground beef nutrition

excerpt: Dry TVP and raw ground beef contain very different amounts of water. Comparing enough of each to provide about 20 g protein makes the trade-offs clearer.
content_html:
TVP often replaces ground beef in tacos, chili and pasta sauce, but TVP is dry while fresh beef contains much more water.

Use the same protein target

The TVP example provides 12 g protein per 23 g dry. Reaching 20 g takes about 38 g dry, roughly 132 calories and 6.7 g fiber. USDA raw 90/10 ground beef provides 20 g protein per 100 g, 176 calories and 10 g fat.

Fiber

Fresh beef has none; the protein-matched dry TVP portion provides roughly 6–7 g.

Fat

Plain defatted TVP can be nearly fat-free before cooking; 90/10 beef contains 10 g fat/100 g, including about 4 g saturated fat.

Micronutrients

Beef naturally supplies B12, zinc and heme iron. Soy contributes other minerals but unfortified TVP is not a dependable B12 source.

Sodium

Both can start relatively low before seasoning; packaged sauces and crumbles can change that.

faq.question: Does TVP have more protein?
faq.answer: Dry TVP is more concentrated; about 38 g dry here provides ~20 g protein, similar to 100 g raw 90/10 beef.

faq.question: Does TVP provide B12?
faq.answer: Not naturally in a dependable amount.
